# <!--name-->edot-release/start-patch<!--/name-->

[![usages](https://img.shields.io/badge/usages-white?logo=githubactions&logoColor=blue)](https://github.com/search?q=elastic%2Foblt-actions%2Fedot-release%2Fstart-patch+%28path%3A.github%2Fworkflows+OR+path%3A**%2Faction.yml+OR+path%3A**%2Faction.yaml%29&type=code)
[![test-edot-release-start-patch](https://github.com/elastic/oblt-actions/actions/workflows/test-edot-release-start-patch.yml/badge.svg?branch=main)](https://github.com/elastic/oblt-actions/actions/workflows/test-edot-release-start-patch.yml)

<!--description-->
Cut the EDOT patch branch patching/X.Y.Z from the highest release tag of a line and cherry-pick merged main pull requests onto it. The caller checks out full history and tags and configures the Git identity and credentials.
<!--/description-->

## Inputs

<!--inputs-->
| Name            | Description                                                                                                                                                  | Required | Default                    |
|-----------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------|----------------------------|
| `line`          | Release line to patch, X.Y. The source is its highest release tag.                                                                                           | `true`   | ` `                        |
| `pull-requests` | Squash-merged main pull requests to cherry-pick, as numbers separated by spaces or commas, each with an optional leading #. They are applied in merge order. | `false`  | ` `                        |
| `ref-name`      | Dispatched branch; the action runs only from main.                                                                                                           | `false`  | `${{ github.ref_name }}`   |
| `dry-run`       | true to run every check and cherry-pick and print the push instead of running it. For tests.                                                                 | `false`  | `false`                    |
| `repository`    | GitHub repository of the release and its pull requests.                                                                                                      | `false`  | `${{ github.repository }}` |
| `github-token`  | GitHub token with pull-requests read access for the pull request lookups. The push uses the caller's Git credentials, which need contents write access.      | `false`  | `${{ github.token }}`      |
<!--/inputs-->

## Outputs

<!--outputs-->
| Name            | Description                                                                                              |
|-----------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `branch`        | Patch branch, patching/X.Y.Z. Set in a dry-run too.                                                      |
| `source-tag`    | Release tag the patch branch starts from, with its prefix. Set in a dry-run too.                         |
| `version`       | Version the patch branch will release, X.Y.Z. Set in a dry-run too.                                      |
| `pull-requests` | Applied pull request numbers in merge order, separated by spaces. Empty when none. Set in a dry-run too. |
<!--/outputs-->

## Usage

Dispatch it from `main` with a release line. It resolves the line's highest
release tag, for example `v1.2.3` for line `1.2`, cuts `patching/1.2.4` from
it, cherry-picks the listed pull requests, and pushes the branch once, after
every check and cherry-pick succeeded. Any failure pushes nothing. Later
fixes reach an existing patch branch through pull requests into it.

Only a tag that contains `.github/edot-release.json` can be patched: the
patch branch runs the release workflows of its source tag. The action reads
`tagPrefix` from `.github/edot-release.json` in the checked-out commit; see
[`prepare-start`](../prepare-start/README.md#configuration).

The repository must be checked out with full history and tags. The Git
identity and credentials are the caller's: configure them first, for example
with `elastic/oblt-actions/git/setup` and the same token. The push needs
contents write access. The action does not configure Git itself.

<!--usage action="elastic/oblt-actions/edot-release/start-patch" version="env:VERSION"-->
```yaml
steps:
  - uses: actions/checkout@v7
    with:
      fetch-depth: 0
      token: ${{ steps.token.outputs.token }}
  - uses: elastic/oblt-actions/git/setup@v1
    with:
      github-token: ${{ steps.token.outputs.token }}
  - uses: elastic/oblt-actions/edot-release/start-patch@v1
    with:
      line: ${{ inputs.line }}
      pull-requests: ${{ inputs.pull_requests }}
      github-token: ${{ steps.token.outputs.token }}
```
<!--/usage-->

## Cherry-picks

- Each pull request must be squash-merged into `main`. A pull request whose
  merge commit has more than one parent stops the action. A rebase-merged
  pull request is not detected, and only its last commit would be picked.
- Pull requests are picked in merge order, whatever order they are listed in.
  A pull request listed twice fails as an empty cherry-pick.
- A pull request that does not apply cleanly stops the action with a message
  that names it and the patch branch. Dispatch again without it, then
  cherry-pick it by hand through a pull request into the patch branch.
- Cherry-picks create commits, so they need the caller's Git identity, also
  in a dry-run.
